battle.name: 星川皇子之亂
battle.brief: 公元四七九年冬，雄略天皇崩後留遺詔不許次皇子星川皇子繼位，其母吉備稚媛勸其起兵，星川遂奪平城京大藏省。執政大伴室屋與東漢掬直引兵包圍，縱火焚倉，星川皇子、稚媛與吉備上道君皇子同死火中。卡面秦弩正是大藏省入藏的進口兵刃，叛軍奪倉，奪的就是弓弩存量。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 星川皇子之亂是公元四七九年倭國大和朝廷內部的一場宮廷政變，戰線幾乎全部落在平城京的官署區與宮門一帶。雙方沒有在野外列陣，而是以王宮的倉儲、門禁與街坊為爭奪物。叛軍一方以二皇子星川皇子為首，兵力骨幹是他母親吉備稚媛的娘家吉備上道臣氏，以及大和在地的豪族支持者；起義並無正式編制，依靠的是對宮中財貨與武備存放位置的掌握，以及突發式的奪倉。忠於朝廷的一方是大伴室屋所率的大伴氏集團，室屋當時任大連，是執政級的大臣，握有首都的人事調度與兵權；另有東漢掬直，這位秦氏系的重臣與大伴氏同為雄略天皇指定的遺詔見證人。清寧天皇（時為皇太弟白皇子）站在朝廷一方。整體而言，叛軍缺少律令制下的常備兵力，諸國司也沒有響應；律令制下平城京的兵權分掌於中務省與諸省吏員手中，叛軍並未取得這些編制，近江、越後等地的國司也沒有出兵，事件自始自終局限在首都一隅。而朝廷一方雖然未能阻止火攻帶來的損失，最終仍掌握了首都的門禁與稅收樞紐，完成了平叛。
countriesEn: The Rebellion of Prince Hoshikawa was a court coup fought inside the Yamato government of the Japanese realm in AD 479, with almost the whole front running through the administrative quarter of the Heijō capital and the gates of the imperial palace. The two sides never deployed in the open field; what they fought over was the imperial storehouse, the city gates and the wards of the capital themselves. The rebel side was headed by the second prince, Prince Hoshikawa, and its military backbone was the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan to which his mother, Lady Wakahime of Gibi, belonged, together with local Yamato clan support. The rising had no formal establishment of its own: it relied on knowledge of where the court's money and weapons were stored, and on a sudden seizure of the storehouse. The side loyal to the court was the Ōtomo group under Ōtomo no Muraya, who as a dairen, one of the highest offices of state, controlled the capital's personnel and armed strength. Alongside him stood Higashi no Kana-nao, a senior minister of the Hata clan, who together with Ōtomo no Muraya had been named by Emperor Yūryaku as the witnesses of his will. Emperor Sei'nin, then the crown prince Shiratsuhiko, was on the court's side. On the whole the rebels lacked the standing forces that the ritsuryō system could provide, and the provincial governors did not join them: under the ritsuryō system the armed authority of the Heijō capital was divided among the Ministry of Central Affairs and the officials of the other ministries, and the rebels never gained hold of those establishments, nor did the governors of provinces such as Ōmi or Echigo send troops, so the affair stayed within the capital from beginning to end. The court, though unable to prevent the losses caused by the fire, ended up holding the gates and the fiscal hub of the capital and settled the rebellion.
people: 事件裡的關鍵人物都集中在皇族與兩大豪族之間。雄略天皇病危時留下遺詔，指定由皇太弟白皇子（其後即位為清寧天皇）繼承，並明言不可讓次皇子星川皇子繼位；這道遺詔成為整場衝突的引爆點。星川皇子是雄略天皇與吉備稚媛所生之子，長兄磐城皇子已先他離世，他在皇子中居長，卻被遺詔排除在繼承之外。吉備稚媛出身吉備上道臣氏，與前夫田狹生有一子吉備上道君皇子，母子二人最終一同死在火裡；正是稚媛以遺詔不公勸子起兵。大伴室屋是當時執政的大連，主導了平城京的警戒與包圍，並下令縱火焚燒大藏省。東漢掬直出自秦氏一系，與大伴氏並列為遺詔見證人，其部眾是包圍圈的另一支骨幹。事後主導清算的清寧天皇沒收了吉備上道臣氏所管的山部，把這支曾經能一次派出四十艘軍船的豪族勢力削弱下去。吉備上道臣氏本是從筑紫、備前一帶進入大和的豪族，與大伴氏同列為當時最有力的兩家，事件之後兩家的位置就此逆轉。
peopleEn: The decisive figures of the affair all belonged to the imperial house or to the two great clans. On his deathbed Emperor Yūryaku left a will naming the crown prince Shiratsuhiko, the emperor's younger brother and the man who was to reign as Emperor Sei'nin, and stating expressly that his second prince, Hoshikawa, was not to succeed him; that will became the spark of the whole conflict. Prince Hoshikawa was the son of Yūryaku and Lady Wakahime of Gibi. His elder brother, Prince Yashiro, had died before him, so among the princes he was the eldest, yet the will excluded him from the succession. Lady Wakahime was born into the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan and had borne a son, Prince Kimi no Michi no Omi, by her former husband Tasa; mother and son were to die together in the fire. It was she who urged her son to rise, arguing that the will was unjust. Ōtomo no Muraya, the dairen who governed at the time, directed the cordon and the encirclement in the capital and gave the order to set fire to the Great Storehouse. Higashi no Kana-nao, of the Hata lineage, was the other witness of the will beside Ōtomo, and his men formed a second pillar of the ring. Sei'nin, who presided over the reckoning afterwards, took away the Yama-no-be people from the Gibi clan, weakening a house that had once been able to send forty war-ships to sea at a time. The Gibi no Michi no Omi clan was a great house that had come into Yamato from the regions of Tsukushi and Bizen, standing beside the Ōtomo as one of the two most powerful families of the day; after this affair the position of the two houses was reversed.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩是漢式弩的中國原型：弩機把拉力儲存在機括之中，射手不必像拉弓那樣持續用力，射速與精度都優於徒手拉弓，約在公元前三至二世紀定型，經百濟與朝鮮半島傳入倭國，五世紀的大和豪族兵眾已有可能配備。此次交鋒中，《日本書紀》並未逐件記錄兵器，但衝突的物理核心正是大藏省——律令制八省之一，掌財貨、鹽、米、布帛，也保管甲仗、弓矢與進口兵刃的地方，叛軍奪的正是這樣一座庫房。朝廷一方的近身裝備以竹木製的楯、小型長刀與石上熊摘一類短刀、投槍與弓矢為主，數量靠豪族自身的部曲湊合。放火焚倉需要成桶的水、薪柴與風勢配合，火攻器材與取水工具的調度是那一夜最關鍵的後勤工作。弓矢是這一時代豪族部曲的基本裝備，而秦氏一系歷來以弓技聞名，其弓匠部與楯津具部正是中原弩與製弓技術在倭國落地生根的地方。吉備上道臣氏出動的四十艘軍船，則是這場內亂中少數被明確記錄下來的舟師行動。
kitsEn: The crossbow on the card is the Chinese prototype of the Han crossbow: the trigger mechanism stores the pull inside the stock, so the archer does not have to hold the string under continuous force, and the rate of fire and the accuracy both beat a hand-drawn bow. It took shape around the third to second century BC, reached the Japanese realm through Baekje and the Korean peninsula, and by the fifth century was something the Yamato clan warriors of Yamato could already be issued with. The chronicle does not list the weapons piece by piece for this clash, but the physical heart of the conflict was precisely the Great Storehouse, one of the eight ministries under the ritsuryō system, which held the treasury, salt, rice and cloth and which also kept the armour, the bows and the imported weapons in store. The rebels had seized exactly such a magazine. The close combat equipment of the court side was made up of bamboo and wooden shields, small longswords and short blades of the Sumi-katanagu type, javelins and arrows, the numbers being whatever the clan's own bands could supply. Burning the storehouse down required water in quantity, fuel and a favourable wind, so the muster of fire materials and the drawing of water were the most critical logistical work of that night. Bows and arrows were the basic equipment of a clan band in this age, and the Hata lineage had long been famed for the bow, its bowwrights and shieldmakers being the place where the Chinese crossbow and the craft of bow-making took root in the Japanese realm. The forty war-ships sent out by the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan are among the very few naval operations explicitly recorded for this kind of internal strife.
tactics: 叛軍的戰法是典型的宮廷奪倉：先以近身人數在宮門與坊門一帶製造混亂，再直取大藏省，把官署變成據點、財貨變成軍資，試圖用控制的物資換取時間，等待外勤的豪族部隊靠攏。朝廷方面的應對是三段式：一是封閉平城京各門，斷絕出入；二是集中兵力圍住大藏省，把守軍與叛軍一同圈在建築群內；三是以火攻收束戰局——在夜裡從數面同時放火，把倉廩、廳舍與守軍燒在一起，斷糧、滅火已無意義，等到火勢熄滅，抵抗也隨建築一起燒毀。海上方面，吉備上道臣氏派出的軍船沿瀨戶內海北上，計劃在大和登陸接應，但船隊在途中得知星川皇子已死，隨即掉頭返航，救援與補給線同時斷掉。整場衝突並無正式陣形與戰線，靠的是首都的門禁、街道與倉房本身充當戰線。
tacticsEn: The method of the rebels was a textbook palace seizure: a body of men close at hand created confusion around the palace gates and the ward gates, then struck straight at the Great Storehouse, turning the ministry into a position and the treasury into military supply, in the hope that controlling goods would buy time while the clan's field detachments closed in. The court's response had three stages. First, the gates of the Heijō capital were closed and the flow of people in and out was cut. Second, troops were concentrated around the Great Storehouse, enclosing defenders and rebels alike inside the cluster of buildings. Third, the affair was closed out by fire: from several sides at once, during the night, the granaries, the halls and the men in them were burned together, and once the grain was cut and the fire could no longer be checked, the resistance went with the buildings. At sea, the war-ships dispatched by the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan worked north through the Inland Sea with the intention of landing in Yamato to join the prince, but the fleet learned on the way that Hoshikawa was already dead and turned back, so the relief and the line of supply both broke at once. The whole affair had no formal battle line or formation; the gates, the streets and the storehouses of the capital themselves served as the front.
data: 時間點：公元四七九年，即雄略天皇二十三年。天皇於同年十月病崩，享年四十一；事變起於其後的十一月冬令時節；清寧天皇於翌年四八〇年即位。空間：大藏省位於平城京的官衙區，即今奈良市一帶，戰鬥縱深以宮門、坊門與倉區為限，縱橫不過數條坊路。兵力：書紀只記吉備上道臣氏出兵軍船四十艘，叛軍與朝廷的步卒人數都沒有留下數字，只能確定是數十至數百量級的宮廷部曲規模，未必成軍。建制：大藏省屬律令八省之一，掌財貨、鹽、米、布帛與甲仗；秦弩傳入倭國約在公元三至五世紀之間，與《日本書紀》所述同時代。文字記載主要見《日本書紀》卷二十一，《古事記》全無收錄；近江彌勒時（今滋賀縣米原市）朝妻神社的皇子墓寶篋印塔，被當地當作這場事件的實物見證。
dataEn: The date: AD 479, the twenty-third year of Emperor Yūryaku. The emperor fell ill and died in the tenth month of that year at the age of forty-one; the affair broke out in the eleventh month, in the winter cold that followed; Emperor Sei'nin took the throne in AD 480. The ground: the Great Storehouse stood in the administrative quarter of the Heijō capital, in what is now the city of Nara, and the depth of the fighting was bounded by the palace gates, the ward gates and the warehouse area, a matter of a few ward avenues at most. Numbers of men: the chronicle records only that the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan sent out forty war-ships; the strength of the rebels and of the court in foot soldiers was never written down, and can only be fixed as a body of court retainers numbering in the tens or the hundreds, never a formed army. Establishments: the Great Storehouse was one of the eight ministries of the ritsuryō system, with authority over the treasury, salt, rice, cloth and armour; the Chinese crossbow reached the Japanese realm somewhere between the third and the fifth century AD, contemporaneously with the events the chronicle describes. The written record survives mainly in Book XXI of the Nihon Shoki; the Kojiki contains no trace of it at all. At Asuma Shrine in Mera, in Mibata, present-day Shiga prefecture, the hojuin tower called the Prince's Tomb is treated locally as the material trace of the affair.
cause: 起因有三層。第一層是婚姻造成的權力裂痕：吉備上道臣田狹炫耀妻子稚媛的容色，雄略天皇將田狹外派任那國司，隨後奪其妻為妃，這在豪族眼中既是侮辱，也是對吉備氏政治地位的當眾剝奪。第二層是遺詔：雄略天皇臨終留下遺詔，不可讓星川皇子繼位，而指定皇太弟白皇子，同時把遺詔交給大伴室屋與東漢掬直兩位執政見證，等於把繼承問題提前鎖死。第三層是制度層面的衝突：大藏省握有財貨與甲仗的分配權，能決定誰得到兵與糧，因此當繼承權被排除在外、而自己又掌握物資的一方時，起兵的資本便已具備。稚媛以遺詔所出非公勸子起兵，吉備氏提供舟師與部曲，這場政變本質上是豪族之間對遺詔與物資分配權的爭奪。
causeEn: The causes run in three layers. The first is a breach of power opened by marriage: Tasa of the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan boasted of the beauty of his wife Wakahime, and Emperor Yūryaku sent Tasa off to govern the province of Nara and then took the woman into his own palace as a consort. To the clans this was at once an insult and a public stripping of the Gibi clan's standing. The second layer is the will: on his deathbed Yūryaku left an instrument stating that Hoshikawa must not succeed and naming the crown prince Shiratsuhiko instead, and he placed that instrument in the keeping of two ministers of state, Ōtomo no Muraya and Higashi no Kana-nao, so that the question of succession was locked in advance. The third layer is structural: the Great Storehouse controlled the distribution of goods and armour and therefore decided who received arms and food, so that whoever was shut out of the succession, while already holding the stores, held the means of rising. Wakahime urged her son on the ground that the will was not just, and the Gibi clan supplied boats and retainers. The coup was, at bottom, a struggle between clans over the will and over the authority to allocate goods and arms.
impact: 直接結果是政治權力的重新分配。平城京的政權由大伴室屋一代的大伴氏穩住，執政重心從此長期落在大伴氏手中；清寧天皇得以在四八〇年即位，避免了皇位爭奪演成全面內戰。被壓制的一方付出代價：吉備上道臣氏失去所管的山部，被解除對大和腹地一部民眾的控制，連同那支能一次派出四十艘軍船的海上能力也一併受損，豪族勢力從此退居次位。史料層面上，這件事是《日本書紀》記載的五世紀大和皇位危機中最重要的一件，也是唯一一件以武裝政變收場的案例，也因此成為後世研究吉備氏與大伴氏消長的關鍵案例；同時它提醒讀者，《古事記》完全不收此段，內容很可能出自大伴氏系統的傳承，敘述角度並非中立。近江的皇子墓寶篋印塔，則是今日唯一可指的實物痕跡。
impactEn: The immediate outcome was a redistribution of political power. Control of the Heijō capital was secured by the Ōtomo clan of Ōtomo no Muraya, and the centre of government thereafter lay for a long time with the Ōtomo; Emperor Sei'nin was able to take the throne in AD 480, and a struggle over the succession was prevented from degenerating into a general civil war. The defeated side paid the price: the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan lost the Yama-no-be people it had controlled, was stripped of its hold over part of the Yamato heartland, and lost along with it the naval capacity that had once put forty war-ships to sea, so that the clan receded to a secondary position. In terms of the record, this is the most important of the fifth-century Yamato crises over the succession that the Nihon Shoki preserves, and it has accordingly become a key case study for later work on the rise and decline of the Gibi and Ōtomo clans. It is also the only one of these crises that ended in an armed rising in the capital itself. At the same time it warns the reader that the Kojiki records nothing of it at all, so the account very likely comes down through the Ōtomo tradition and is not written from a neutral standpoint. The hojuin tower known as the Prince's Tomb in Mibata is today the only physical trace that can be pointed to.
result: 政變失敗。星川皇子、其母吉備稚媛與異母兄吉備上道君皇子在包圍與火攻中一同被燒死，大藏省的倉廩與廳舍化為焦土，庫存的財貨與甲仗盡毀，朝廷一方付出的代價是首都核心區的損失與重建的負擔。吉備上道臣氏的四十艘軍船在得知消息後空返，志願與計劃一同落空。事後清寧天皇譴責吉備上道臣氏，收回山部，把這支豪族從大和的核心位置驅逐出去；大伴室屋與東漢掬直則因平亂成為新的權力核心。史家留下的疑問同樣明確：這場衝突的規模、兵員與損失數字都沒有留下記錄，事件細節幾乎全部出自一方家族的傳承與後世史家的解讀，書紀把平亂寫成輕鬆而有序的過程，這種敘述更像是勝方留下的秩序，而不是戰場本身的樣子。
resultEn: The coup failed. Prince Hoshikawa, his mother Lady Wakahime of Gibi and his half-brother Prince Kimi no Michi no Omi were all burnt to death in the encirclement and the fire; the granaries and halls of the Great Storehouse were reduced to charred ruins and the stock of goods and armour was destroyed, while the court paid for the affair in damage to the core of the capital and in the burden of rebuilding. The forty war-ships of the Gibi no Michi no Omi clan turned back empty once they learned what had happened, and their purpose and their plans failed together. Afterwards Emperor Sei'nin reproached the Gibi clan and took back the Yama-no-be, driving that house out of its central place in Yamato, while Ōtomo no Muraya and Higashi no Kana-nao became the new core of power as the men who had put the affair down. The questions left by the historians are just as clear: no figures survive for the scale of the conflict, for the numbers of men involved or for the losses, and the details of the affair come almost entirely from the tradition of one family together with the interpretation of later scholars. The chronicle renders the suppression as an easy and orderly business, and that narrative reads more like the order left behind by the winners than like what the fighting was actually like.
